revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Nakai's Savings Account
revealWordProblem.text:
Nakai opened a savings account with an initial deposit, or principal, of $750. The account earns 3.5% simple interest each year. Interest is the amount paid or earned for the use of the principal, and it is called simple interest when it is figured only on the principal. The graph shows the interest Nakai has earned over time.
Question: What observations can you make about the data using the graph?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A phone screen showing a Main Bank Mobile savings account graph of interest earned in dollars against number of years, with points rising in a straight line from 0 to about 105.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The points lie on a straight line through the origin, so the interest grows at a steady rate — the same amount is added each year. Reading the graph, one year earns about $26, two years about $52, three years about $79, and four years about $105, so each year adds roughly $26. That matches the numbers: 3.5% of $750 is 0.035 × 750 = $26.25 a year. Because the line passes through (0, 0), earning nothing in zero years, the relationship can be written as i = 26.25y, where y is the number of years and i is the interest earned. Extending the line predicts about $131 after 5 years.

choiceFeedback: 51 is not three times the rate. Every row runs 48 fans per trip, so three trips carry three times 48.
